title: TelemetryData
description: Parsed telemetry published to the topic exchange RABBITMQ_TELEMETRY_EXCHANGE (default "pact.telemetry") with routing key pact.telemetry.{version-major}.{device-id}. Field order and units mirror buildTelemetryPayload() in the device firmware (tcp.h); firmware_parity_test.go enforces that.

id.description: Device ID: the firmware's 10 raw bytes (up to 6 from DEVICE_MODEL with dashes stripped, then 4 from the short serial, zero-padded) formatted as XXX-XXX-XXXX

version.description: Version nibble (bits 0-3) of the payload flags byte, rendered as a decimal string. Only "0" is accepted by the ingest service

flags.description: Raw flags byte: bits 0-3 version, bit 4 reserved, bit 5 raw ADC fields present, bit 6 cell block present, bit 7 GPS block present

readings.description: Sensor samples ordered oldest to newest. The firmware batches at most MAX_READINGS_PER_PAYLOAD (24) per message; the parser accepts up to the 255 the count byte allows

has_raw.description: True when the payload carried methane_raw and moisture_raw in every record (flags bit 5). When false, both fields are absent from every reading

has_gps.description: True when the payload carried a GPS block (flags bit 7)

latitude.description: Degrees; wire value is int32 scaled by 1e7. The firmware computes the scaled value in float32, so expect roughly 0.2-1 m of quantisation error

longitude.description: Degrees; wire value is int32 scaled by 1e7. Same float32 quantisation as latitude

has_cell.description: True when the payload carried a cell block (flags bit 6)

mobile_network_code.description: MNC 0 is a valid network code and is published as 0, not omitted

timestamp.description: Unix seconds. The newest reading carries an absolute timestamp on the wire; older readings are reconstructed by walking timedif backwards from it

timedif.description: Raw wire value, passed through unchanged. For every reading except the newest it is the gap in seconds to the NEXT NEWER reading. On the newest reading the firmware instead writes the gap to the PREVIOUS OLDER reading (duplicating that reading's timedif), and 0 when the batch holds a single reading. A value of 65535 may be a saturated clamp rather than a true gap, in which case reconstructed timestamps for older readings are too recent

temperature.description: Celsius; wire value is int16 centi-degrees divided by 100, so always an exact hundredth

humidity.description: Percent; wire value is uint16 centi-percent divided by 100

methane_raw.description: Uncalibrated sensor count. Present only when has_raw is true

depth.description: Millimetres. This is the field the firmware calls `distance`; the two names refer to the same wire slot

moisture.description: Percent; wire value is uint16 centi-percent divided by 100

moisture_raw.description: Uncalibrated sensor count. Present only when has_raw is true

battery_percentage.description: Percent; wire value is uint16 centi-percent divided by 100

status.description: Raw sensor-health bitfield from the firmware's TelemetryStatus namespace. 0 means every sensor read succeeded

status_flags.description: `status` decoded into names. Empty when status is 0. A set flag means that sensor's read failed and the corresponding value in this reading is a stale carry-over of the previous sample, not a fresh measurement

anyOf.description: A status bit the firmware has defined but this service does not name yet
